modifications: Renamed from generate-cicd to oss-ci on migration into oss-kit.

Body split by forge: SKILL.md now holds only the forge-independent process (detect the ecosystem, decide what runs, choose a matrix, decide caching), and syntax moved out into references/github-actions.md and a new references/gitlab.md.

references/best-practices.md renamed to references/github-actions.md and rewritten: its Security section was removed because that content belongs to oss-harden (the SEC rules), concrete YAML examples for triggers, matrix, cache keying, timeout, and cancellation were added so the file actually backs the R-CI-* rules it is cited against, and it now states the boundary with oss-harden and oss-publish explicitly.

references/gitlab.md added: GitLab CI/CD syntax for the same decisions (workflow:rules, parallel:matrix, cache:key:files, timeout, interruptible, artifacts:reports:junit), each keyword checked against the current GitLab CI/CD YAML reference before being written.
Added a Scope section and a 'Rules this skill owns' section citing R-CI-01 through R-CI-05 from oss-kit's STANDARD.md.

Code review corrections, both reference files, verified against current vendor documentation: gitlab.md caches .npm/ with npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline instead of a node_modules cache that npm ci empties, documents workflow:auto_cancel:on_new_commit and workflow:rules:auto_cancel as the YAML path for auto-cancellation, states the cache:key:files two-file limit and lack of variable expansion, corrects sast to GitLab Free with advanced features gated to Ultimate, corrects the uses: equivalence claim to name CI/CD components, and drops the R-CI-02 citation and baked-in reporter flags from the test-reports example; github-actions.md replaces an unparseable secrets context reference in a step if: with the env: promotion pattern and replaces <pinned-sha> placeholders with a version tag plus a comment noting oss-harden pins the SHA.

Both reference files gained a static-site deployment section, GitHub Pages and GitLab Pages, checked against each vendor's current documentation on 2026-07-27. It carries no rule ID, because no rule in STANDARD.md requires a project to publish a site, and Step 3 now asks before writing one. Recorded there: GitHub documents pages: write and id-token: write on the deploying job, while its own starter workflow grants both at the top level and so violates R-SEC-02; a Pages deployment inverts R-CI-05's cancellation guidance on both forges; and GitHub ignores a CNAME file entirely when publishing from a custom Actions workflow, so a custom domain is a settings-only change.

Cache policy now prefers official setup-action caching, hashes lockfiles, separates compatibility boundaries, and treats stale fallback restoration as optional because GitHub defines restore-keys as stale-cache prefixes. Matrix coverage now follows every supported release line, applicable project checks replace a mandatory lint-test-build trio, and GitLab no longer cancels diagnostic jobs on the first failure.
